newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria-British trade rises 50 pct in Jan-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria-British trade rises 50 pct in Jan-Sept.

text.p: Nigeria imported goods and services from Britain worth 500 million stg in the first nine months of 1996, some 50 percent above the same period last year, said the head of a British trade delegation to Nigeria on Wednesday.
John Dorrell of the Kent trade mission touring Nigeria told the News Agency of Nigeria that exports from Nigeria to Britain during the period amounted to more than 300 million stg.
Dorrell said there were big prospects for business transactions between the two countries.
"There is a high demand for British products in Nigeria," he said.

Trade between Nigeria and its former colonial power, Britain fell following the annulment of a presidential election in 1993 in the populous oil-rich African nation that would have restored democracy.

The Nigerian economy took a battering as the annulment plunged the country into political turmoil but a combination of free market and tight fiscal policies in place since last year has stabilised key sectors of the economy and tamed inflation.
Dorrell said six of the 16-member trade mission had already made prospective business contacts.

"Some are here to do market research, some already know the market but have come to see if their products would meet the demand of Nigerians while others are already doing business with Nigerians," he said.
The mission arrived in Nigeria from Atlanta, United States last Saturday for a week's tour and will proceed to Accra, Ghana this weekend.
